problem_summary.summary: Count the nodes in a complete binary tree, whose final level is filled from left to right.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: root of a guaranteed-complete binary tree. Return its node count.
constraints: Requested algorithm should be faster than O(n)

brute_force.explanation: Traverse every node with a queue and increment a counter.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every reachable node is enqueued exactly once, so the counter equals the total node count when the queue is empty.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(w) auxiliary for the breadth-first queue.

optimized.explanation: Compare the heights of the leftmost paths in the left and right subtrees. If equal, the left subtree is perfect; otherwise the right subtree is perfect. Count a perfect subtree directly and recurse only into the incomplete side.
optimized.correctness_idea: Completeness guarantees that at least one of the two child subtrees of any node is perfect. A perfect subtree of height h contains 2^h - 1 nodes, so each recursive step counts one full side and descends into the only potentially incomplete side.
optimized.time_complexity: O(log^2 n) — each of O(log n) recursive levels measures paths of O(log n) length.
optimized.space_complexity: O(log n) auxiliary recursion stack for a complete tree.

steps.event: Measure child leftmost heights at root 1.
steps.condition: Equal heights mean the left subtree rooted at 2 is perfect.
steps.action: Count root plus the left subtree as 2^2 = 4; recurse right.

steps.condition: Heights differ, so the empty right subtree is perfect.
steps.action: Count node 3 as 1; recurse into left child 6.

steps.condition: All six nodes have been counted exactly once.

edge_cases.handling: Equal child heights allow each subtree count to be computed directly.

edge_cases.case: Last level has only its leftmost node
edge_cases.handling: The unequal-height branch recurses into the left side and counts the perfect right side.
